_README: G1's tracked ledger (docs/handoff-playable.md §6.5). ONE entry per landed rung.
Every number here was measured by the harness named in `how`, in the session that wrote
the entry. A number without a `how` is not a number -- delete it rather than carry it.
THE METRIC IS `median_warm` (§0). The gate viewpoints are worst cases and sit between p90
and p99; quoting one as 'the frame' overstates the typical frame by ~1.5-1.9x.

entries.what: THE DIRTY CENSUS -- how much of the image does one frame actually change?
entries.negative_control: two pristine images walked in full (68,223,650 words): 0 differ
entries.cross_check: the four frames' op counts (52194203/44260279/47671745/41812643) reproduce the certified gate figures to the digit -- the binary wire drove the real frames
entries.VERDICT: The ~52ms blanket memcpy is ~99.99% waste. 216 ranges / 0.22 MB would replace 546 MB (~2400x fewer bytes); even a crude 41-range 28 MB superset is ~19x. The four per-frame sets overlap heavily (6,685 union vs 17,490 if disjoint), so the dirty region is largely the SAME region each frame -- what a static bound needs.
NOT_ESTABLISHED: This measured the dirty SET, not a working restore. The sub-millisecond reset is arithmetic from bytes-moved, NOT a measured reset time; per-range overhead is unmodelled. That is B4.1 step 2 (change fastrun's reset path and re-time it).
All four frames are keys=0. A MOVING tic runs the sim and writes player state and may dirty more. 6s per frame to check -- do it before designing the mechanism.
entries.CONSEQUENCE: If the floor collapses, frame time is ops-bound again and Step A's wins convert fully. At 300M fj/s the 27.72M median is ~92ms (~10.8 fps) with a free reset, so 30 fps needs roughly a 10M-op frame. docs/handoff-playable.md §4.2's 'a fixed ~52ms no amount of Step A removes' is retired as a PERMANENT constraint.
entries.tool_note: The exact walk costs 6 SECONDS per pass, not the minutes assumed -- the sampler and its confidence interval were never necessary. Prefer --exact.

entries.what: The two confirmed fractional-position mirror divergences, FIXED. Both were byte-exactness breaks invisible to every gate because all certified viewpoints sit on whole map units.

PJ-1.bug: proj.wedge_setup builds the eye terms at full 16.16 and readers slice the high nibbles = floor(viewy-viewx); mapcompiler.bbox_wedge_miss floored PER AXIS = floor(viewy)-floor(viewx). Differ by 1 on borrow (q=1) / carry (q=3).
PJ-1.fix: THE ORACLE MOVED, not fj. mapcompiler.bbox_wedge_miss now floors after combining, with the 16.16 eye threaded through visible_segs/bsp_render_order.
PJ-1.why_this_direction: Only floor-after-combining is CONSERVATIVE: Q - Q_true = frac(E) in [0,1) for all four q, so a cull always implies the true point is outside. Per-axis flooring gives q=3 an error of fx+fy in [0,2), so Q=1 on the negated plane m=3 culls a box that is genuinely INSIDE -- and the wedge has ZERO angular slack at view angles that are exact multiples of 45 degrees, two of which are certified gate angles. ⚠ MY FIRST ATTEMPT WENT THE OTHER WAY and I had written the (false) claim that both forms are conservative into the source; the fan-out sweep caught it.
PJ-1.fj_cost: ZERO -- fj emission unchanged by PJ-1 (walk stayed 73,957 lines)
PJ-1.proof: scratchpad/_pj1_probe.py: fj 120/120 agree, per-axis 110/10. Roles INVERTED vs before the fix, which is itself the regression test.

PJ-2.bug: sgn = -fixed_mul_lo(a, |viewx|) truncates toward zero; the oracle's fixed_mul floors. Equal iff P mod 2^16 == 0, i.e. only at a whole map unit.
PJ-2.fix: fj multiplies the SIGNED value, at THREE sites: projection.fj wall_x_range + wall_x_range_m, and frame_render.fj seg_pass1_leaf_body_proj -- the third was NOT in the CR finding and is the 'fixed in one macro, not its twin' shape that let the M14-c bug survive.
PJ-2.forced_fanout: flipjump warns on an UNUSED MACRO PARAMETER and the build is --werror, so the 4 dead abs/sign params could not be left in place: 2 signatures, 2 bodies, 2 dead @-locals, 19 frame_render lines (9 calls + 10 scope lists), 12 emitter statements + 4 labels, 7 test heads + 7 decls, 1 test call, 2 harnesses. Safe on rule 4 because NO Python f-string emits these calls (grep over src/doomfj/).
PJ-2.proof: scratchpad/_pj2_probe.py: signed 10/10, abs/negate 5/10 (every divergence +1 ULP). Control 6 MEASURES that the row-rule operand swap is bit-identical rather than assuming it. R17 trap confirmed: even `a` at a half unit agrees, odd `a` differs.

entries.what: The dirty-range restore: MEASURED. The prize is real; the naive mechanism is REFUTED.

THE_PRIZE_CONFIRMED.note: Per-range call overhead is NEGLIGIBLE -- 234 Python->C set_words calls cost 0.12 ms total, so the bytes-moved reduction converts almost perfectly. The ~45ms floor really can become ~0.1ms.

THE_MECHANISM_REFUTED.finding: A range set LEARNED FROM SAMPLED FRAMES IS UNSOUND. 5 of 7 unseen frames leaked with a 5-frame learn set; with 30 learn frames the union grew 6,880 -> 9,225 and op-level leaks fell to 1 of 7, but the EXACT WALK still found 67 and 2 unrestored words. It converges slowly and does not close.
THE_MECHANISM_REFUTED.why_it_matters: The program SELF-MODIFIES, so a leaked word does not produce a wrong pixel -- it produces a different PROGRAM. Op deltas ranged +3 to +4,375,384.
THE_MECHANISM_REFUTED.PIXELS_ARE_NOT_A_DETECTOR: pixels MATCHED on ALL 7 frames in BOTH runs, including the one that leaked 4.4M ops. A pixel-only validation would have passed every case and shipped a broken restore.
THE_MECHANISM_REFUTED.OPS_ARE_NOT_A_COMPLETE_DETECTOR_EITHER: the (-416,256,k=4) frame matched op-for-op (+0) while the exact walk still found 2 unrestored words. The FULL WALK is the only sound check.
THE_MECHANISM_REFUTED.the_leaks_are_STRUCTURED: the same addresses recur across runs (3304301, 5511717, 5649875, 5649877, 5753831, ...), so the writable set is a structured region, not noise -- it is simply not enumerable by sampling.

entries.RECOMMENDED_MECHANISM: Derive the writable set from the EMITTER, which knows every address the program can write (state cells, thing rows, bindings, banks, per-frame scratch), and emit it as a manifest next to the program. scratchpad/dirty_restore.py then becomes its ACCEPTANCE TEST: learn nothing, restore the manifest's ranges, and require 0 unrestored words on the full walk over a wide frame set. Alternative: engine-side write tracking in the C core (sound by construction, but a flipjump change).

BLOCKER_FOUND_IN_PASSING.R4: the M14 tier is 68,213,458 words -- 1.6% OVER the certified 2**26 flat limit. At 1<<26 it runs in HYBRID storage, and `freeze()` requires PURE FLAT, so THE FAST RESET PATH IS UNAVAILABLE TO THE TIER THAT WILL SHIP. Op counts are identical in both modes (43,115,656), so no earlier measurement is invalidated. Only at 1<<27 is it flat. R4 says no silent paged-mode fallback -- this needs a decision before B0, and it competes with B3's 9-level span budget (G3).
